articleTitle: A Low Spur Injection Locking Oscillator with Secondary Injection Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Pulse injection locking technique can effectively extends the phase-locked loop bandwidth to suppress phase noise of ring oscillators. However, due to its instantaneous phase correction, the spur performance of injection locking oscillators (ILOs) are sensitive to the frequency deviation between free-running oscillating frequency and injection frequency. The spurs performance if ILOs are far inferior to conventional Type-II phase-locked loops (PLLs), which limit their application which limits their application in the field of communication. In this paper a secondary injection technology is proposed to improve the spur performance by smoothing the phase correction amplitude. In the proposed secondary injection oscillator, two ring oscillators with the same self-resonant frequency connected with a small size inverter. The reference pulse only inject to the first oscillator, and the phase noise of second oscillator can also be suppressed by optimized circuit design. Meanwhile, the phase correction can occurs at every period rather than instantaneously in the second oscillator. A quadrature ILO with 2.3 GHz ~ 2.6 GHz frequency tuning range is designed on 40nm CMOS process to verified the proposed technology. Simulation results shows that the phase correction amplitude can be significantly reduced. The reference spur performance improve from -59dBc to -69dBc with 100MHz input, 2.5GHz output and 150KHz frequency deviation. The proposed secondary injection oscillator achieves - 127.8 dBc/Hz @ 10MHz phase noise with a 1.1V supply consuming 12.14mW.

articleTitle: A Low-Power 40Gb/s PAM4 Transmitter with High Speed-Latch and 3-Tap FFE
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This article designs a low power high-speed Latch and 3-tap FFE (Feed forward Equalizer) circuit for the 40GB/s PAM4 Signal SerDes system, which is applied to the sender. On the basis of in-depth learning and exploration of the principles of multiplexers (MUX) and FFE in SerDes, the UMC28nm process and 1.05V power supply voltage are adopted. By improving the high-speed Latch application in the 3Latch structure and adopting half rate technology, the power consumption can be reduced by about 70%. By configuring the FFE tap coefficient to reduce ISI (Inter Code Interference), a configurable 3-tap FFE is designed that can be applied to backplane links with medium to low losses (OdB<loss<20dB), Finally, under various PVT conditions, four 10Gb/s NRZ signals are generated into one 40 Gb/s PAM4 signal, with a 4:2 MUX and 3-tap FFE circuit with a power consumption of 49mW.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Calibration Technique for Bit-Weight Errors in Pipelined-SAR ADCs
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a calibration technique for capacitor mismatches and inter-stage gain error in a pipelined-SAR ADC. Foreground calibration scheme is employed for capacitor mismatches that are immune to voltage-temperature (VT) variations while a background calibration method is used to obtain the coefficient of the inter-stage gain. The proposed hybrid calibration technique is independent of the input signal distribution. Moreover, common mode voltage can be avoided by splitting the capacitors in the digital-to-analog-converter (DAC), thereby saving hardware while maintaining the calibration accuracy. The residue voltage swings are the same in both foreground and background calibration modes through the use of a split switching method, and hence the inter-stage amplifier linearity is not degraded. Simulation results show that, based on 14-bit 100MS/s pipelined-SAR ADC structure, the spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) can reach l08.5dbc and signal to interference plus noise ratio (SNR) can reach 85.7db after using the proposed calibration method.

articleTitle: A Novel Tempreature-Included CSWPL Model for GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel temperature-included canonical section-wise piecewise linear (CSWPL) behavioral model. The basic theory of the CSWPL model and the proposed modeling method are described in detail. A 10 W gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) provided by Wolfspeed is used for comprehensive simulation tests. A comparison is made between the proposed model and the classical temperature-dependent CSWPL model. As a result of the developed model, accurate predictions can be made over a wide range of ambient temperatures (-20°C to 130°C) and input powers. Additionally, load-pull simulation results are presented, which demonstrate that the proposed model is able to accurately predict the output power contour as well as the power-added efficiency contour.

articleTitle: A Sensorless MPPT Structure for Low Cost Solar Energy Harvesting in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is necessary for efficient solar energy harvesting. In the context of wireless sensor networks (WSNs), MPPT often makes use of sensors to aid in calculating the maximum power point voltage of solar panel. However, existing methods are susceptible to changes in environmental conditions and system parameters and are unable to handle the complex and dynamic application scenarios for WSNs. In this paper, a sensorless MPPT structure is proposed which uses the solar panel for energy harvesting itself as the sensor and employs simple circuit structure and control flow to execute MPPT. Experimental results show that in terms of energy harvesting efficiency, the proposed structure performs better than existing ones.

articleTitle: Enabling Efficient Bayesian Convolutional Neural Network with Feature Pre-extraction and Pre-pooling Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Introducing Bayesian method into convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can effectively prevent neural networks from making over-confident decisions and overfitting. However, the large number of parameters in Bayesian convolutional neural networks (BCNNs) results in high computational costs, limiting the deployment in resource-sensitive computing systems. In this paper, two efficient strategies for BCNNs are proposed to optimize the inference process: 1) Feature Pre-extraction (F-P) strategy, which pre-extracts the feature maps in convolutional layers to reduce redundant computation introduced by repeated calculation, and 2) Pre-pooling (P-P) strategy, which performs pooling in advance to reduce the scale of feature maps involved in subsequent calculations. Compared with current efficient BCNN inference model, F-P strategy can eliminate around 92 % multiplications and accumulations, and P-P strategy can save 75% Gaussian random numbers requirement. To sum up, the proposed two optimization strategies can enable BCNN to save around 93% computational resources with 30.6% memory overhead together. The accuracy of LeNet-5 on CIFAR10 dataset has slightly decreased by 0.1%.

articleTitle: Analysis and Implementation of Staggered Wire Bonding for LVDS Data and Large Power Transmission in CMOS Image Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel structure of staggered pad configuration for wire bonding to simultaneously transmit Low-Voltage Differential Signaling (LVDS) data and large power for ultra-high speed global shutter(GS) CMOS image sensor(CIS). In this structure, the inner pads are high-density placed close to the pixel array to achieve large power transmission and small IR drop. The outer pads are low-density placed in the outer area of the chip with independent power ring and power pad to transmit the LVDS data and remove the interference between the CIS power line and LVDS circuit. Noise impact of power line on the LVDS signal line has been modeled, analyzed and simulated. A prototype GS CIS chip with the proposed structure has been fabricated in a 110nm CIS process. The measurement results show that the chip can provide large power of 9.7 W to the CIS and transmit LVDS data at speed of 250Mbps per channel.

articleTitle: Design of Energy Efficient Logarithmic Approximate Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient logarithm approximate multiplier architecture is proposed. The proposed architecture is designed based on the Mitchell approximate multiplier. Several novel design methods are proposed to make the multiplier more energy efficient while maintaining acceptable computation accuracy. In order to improve the efficiency of the computation, the operands are truncated and the right shifter in the logarithm-to-binary converter is removed in the proposed design. While iterative method is used to compensate for approximation errors, approximate adder is used during error compensation to reduce the complexity of the compensation circuit. A novel error metric is also proposed to evaluate the accumulated error effects of approximate multipliers in real applications. Compared with the conventional Mitchell approximate multiplier, the proposed design can achieve a 56.1% smaller delay, a 23.9% smaller area and a 65.9% smaller power-delay product (PDP) while its approximation error is reduced. Case studies of image processing and K-means clustering are used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Design Method OF RF Frontend Based on Interferometer Direction Finding Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a RF front-end design idea based on interferometer direction finding technology, using planar spiral antenna, bandwidth spliced frequency conversion circuit and broadband AD circuit to realize the real-time reception of 12GHz frequency bandwidth,and improves the interception probability, direction finding accuracy and receiving sensitivity of conventional direction finding system. In this paper, four 3GHz bandwidth splicing are used to realize the instantaneous direction finding of 12GHz bandwidth, and skillfully combine power division network and millimeter wave mixing circuit to achieve ultra-low spurious and high harmonic suppression transmission of broadband signals. The scheme can achieve azimuth coverage of airspace is 45°, pitch-15° ~+70°, Real-time receiving 12GHz wide bandwidth signal. The direction finding accuracy can be better than 1°.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation of Peak Detection Algorithm for X-Ray Fluorescence Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: X-ray fluorescence (XRF) is the emission of characteristic “secondary” X-rays from a material that has been excited by high-energy X-rays. X-ray fluorescence systems are widely used for elemental and chemical analyses. In XRF systems, various techniques have been developed for the synthesis of pulse shapes using digital methods instead of traditional analog methods. The accuracy of XRF spectrometers can be improved using an appropriate trapezoidal pulse shaping method. In this paper, an efficient trapezoidal filter architecture is presented. In addition, we present a hardware-efficient peak value detection algorithm. By using the proposed algorithm, the peak value detection error is decreased up to 53.1% compared with the conventional algorithm. The proposed design was implemented on Altera Cyclone IV FPGA and successfully operated.

articleTitle: Power Consumption Benchmarking of TinyOS Applications with A Dedicated Measurement Adapter
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks need to operate as long as possible under battery power, which makes reducing node power consumption a primary design goal for wireless sensor networks. In order to better understand power consumption characteristics of sensor nodes, it is necessary to establish power consumption benchmarking for typical example applications. To achieve this goal, this paper designs a dedicated adapter board for power measurement and uses it to perform power consumption tests on typical TinyOS example applications. Experimental results show that using the proposed adapter, not only can the overall power consumption of sample applications be quickly analyzed, but also the details of voltage and current changes can be deeply understood.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Microsystem SiP for on-Board Embedded Computer
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: The miniaturization and lightweight requirements faced by OBCs (on-board control computers) are becoming increasingly urgent. As high-density packaging method, System in Package (SiP) is able to compress multiple functions into smaller external dimensions, conforming to high integration and high performance requirements of military electronics. Aiming at the demand for high-density, high-performance and miniaturization of components used in spacecraft, an embedded microcomputer SiP for aerospace applications has been designed in this paper. System design and layout design of the SiP is introduced. Electrical, thermal, and mechanical simulations have been conducted to ensure design rationality and design reliability, and the simulation results shows that the SiP satisfy all the requirements for orbit flight. The outline dimension of the SiP is only 31mm*31mm*10mm, and the weight of overall module is about 20g. Compared to PCB design, the volume and weight are reduced by 70%. The embedded microcomputer SiP satisfies the performance requirements and size requirements of onboard computers.

articleTitle: A Resource-efficient FIR Filter Design Based on an RAG Improved Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In modern digital filter chip design, efficient resource utilization is a hot topic. Due to linear phase characteristics of FIR filters, a pulsed fully parallel structure can be applied to attack the problem. In order to further reduce hardware resource consumption especially caused by multiplication function, an improved RAG algorithm is proposed. Filters with different orders and for different algorithms are compared, and the experimental results show that the improved RAG algorithm is excellent in terms of logic resource utilization, resource allocation, running speed, and power consumption under different application scenarios. The proposed algorithm invokes a better circuit structure for FIR filter, it gives full play to resource allocation strategy and reduces logic resource consumption. The proposed circuit is faster and more stable, and suitable for a variety of complex application scenarios.

articleTitle: A 2.1pJ/bit 56-Gb/s PAM-4 CDR with Integrated AFE in 28nm CMOS for Direct-Modulated Laser Drivers
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a 56-Gb/s PAM-4 reference-less bang-bang clock and data recovery circuit (CDR) with an analog front-end (AFE) for direct-modulate laser drivers applications. A quarter-rate structured CDR has been implemented, along with the integration of transition selection functionality to handle the locking of CDR for PAM-4 signals. Furthermore, a dynamic comparator has been introduced, capable of comparing, demultiplexing, and thermometer encoding PAM-4 signal levels. The proposed CDR has been implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process, achieving an energy efficiency of 2.1 pJ/bit. The recovered 7 GHz clock displays an integrated jitter of 1.43 ps across a 1 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Dual-Comparator based Low-Cost Low-Ripple Buck DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: A dual-comparator based low-cost low-ripple buck DC-DC converter is designed in 65-nm CMOS, with a quiescent current of 38 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{A}$</tex>. By using digital switches and a multiplexing comparator, the error comparator and peak-voltage comparator are combined into a single module with low complexity. The input voltage of 3.3 V is converted to an output voltage of 1.5 V, with the peak efficiency of 94% and load regulation of 0.15%, under the load current changes from 1 mA to 50 mA. The circuit is simple and only includes logic control, power driver, power stage, multiplexing module and zero-voltage comparator. The proposed converter has a maximum output ripple of 5.7 mV under <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 10\%$</tex> supply variations, -40-90 °C temperature range and different process corners.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Chiplet Solution for Non-volatile In-memory Computing Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In order to overcome the memory wall problem, academia and industry have proposed AI accelerator architecture based on non-volatile in-memory computing (IMC) devices. However, this computing architecture has a low utilization rate of hardware resources, resulting in a large amount of buffer and memory computing device resource waste. Therefore, in order to better compatible with traditional convolutional neural networks and improve the utilization of hardware resources, this paper proposes a heterogeneous chiplet solution. This solution tries to meet the requirements of the size and depth of the feature map of different layers in the same convolutional neural network model for hardware resources, and greatly increases the utilization rate of hardware resources. Compared with the homogeneous solution, this solution improves the utilization rate of buffer resources by more than 50 %, and the increase of latency can be ignored.

articleTitle: A GaN-Based Unipolar Sinusoidal Pulse-Width Modulated Inverter with High Efficiency and High Power
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This brief presents a high-power, high-efficiency GaN-based unipolar sinusoidal pulse-width modulated inverter. The comparator is the core of the inverter and the modulation process is dependent on the comparator. Designed depletion-mode (DM) GaN comparator exhibits excellent performances. On-chip experimental results show that the DM GaN comparator can operate up to 2 MHz with full waveform integrity and no distortion using 0.25μm GaN-on-Si process technology. The simulation results of the inverter based on the designed comparator are as follows: the inverter produces up to 16.9W of output power, 84% efficiency of power stage, 74% efficiency of the entire circuit and the total harmonic distortion rate (THD) is 0.75%. The proposed novel inverter implements sinusoidal pulse-width modulation in DC-AC conversion process.

articleTitle: High Energy-efficient Change Detection Method for Video Surveillance with Approximate Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Video surveillance is widely used for security monitoring of important infrastructure such as highways and electricity facilities. With the development of new technologies and limitations in transmission bandwidth, some functions need to be deployed on edge devices, increasing the demand for computational power. As a typical fault-tolerant application, video surveillance can be designed to be lightweight using approximate computing techniques. This paper focuses on the fundamental function of change detection in video surveillance and presents an approximate hardware implementation of the change detection based on principal component analysis (PCA) and K-means algorithm. Experimental results show that the approximate change detection method produces results with extremely small differences compared to precise calculations, while reducing the hardware area overhead of the core operator by over 40%.

articleTitle: Output Truncation Realization of a Filter with Variable Decimation Factor
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Digital decimation filters are a critical component of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma\Delta \text{ADC}$</tex>, but their large number of digital units can result in high area and power consumption, which can significantly impact the entire ADC. To address this issue, this paper proposes a digital filter output truncation method applied to variable decimation multiples of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma\Delta \text{ADC}$</tex>. By selectively truncating the effective bits of each stage filter while ensuring accuracy, the proposed method reduces the use of register resources, thereby reducing the area and power consumption of the digital decimation filter. The filter used in this study consists of three stages: cascaded integrator-comb filter(CIC), compensation filter, and half-band filter. Simulation results and analysis demonstrate that this truncation method with a 16-bit output bit width achieves an ENOB of 15.4 and reduces the adder's computational workload by 46.7% compared to non-truncation.

articleTitle: A Switched Capacitor Based Capacitance Measurement Method for Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a integrated circuits capacitance measurement method based on switched capacitor circuits. Compared with other capacitance measurement methods, simple circuit design and wide measurement range are the mainly advantages. The whole circuit is designed using 45nm CMOS standard componments, which allows it to be BIST method for contemporary integrated circuits. The HSPICE simulation and practical experiment show that the proposed method can measure the capacitance ranged from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10 fF$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$80pF$</tex> with measurement deviation less than 1.5%.

articleTitle: Study of Degradation Mechanisms in Hydrogen-Terminated Diamond MOSFETs Under Off-State and Semi-on-State Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: The study of degradation mechanisms is important to improve the reliability of hydrogen-terminated (C-H) diamond metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs). In this article, the trapping effects of C-H diamond MOSFET under off-state and semi-on-state conditions are studied by pulsed characterization. The results show that the on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{\text{ON}})$</tex> increase with the increased intensity of the drain quiescent bias (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DSQ</inf>) under off-state conditions; the further increase in RON under semi-on-state conditions due to the hot-carrier effects. Furthermore, under off-state conditions, the increase in threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>) is mainly due to the reverse gate quiescent bias (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GSQ</inf>) and the increased intensity in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DSQ</inf>, which promotes the detrapping effects under the gate region. In addition, the decrease in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{TH}}$</tex> under semi-on-state conditions is caused by the weakness of detrapping effects and the enhancement of hot-carrier effects.

articleTitle: A 1.8μA, 202 ns Fast Transient Response Output Capacitor-Less LDO with Dual Power Transistors
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, an output capacitor-less low dropout (LDO) regulator with low power consumption and fast transient response is proposed. The dual power transistors are adaptively activated based on the load current. Furthermore, dynamic biasing techniques are utilized to enhance the response speed of the error amplifier. During transient response, the dynamic current is increased by adjusting the resistance of the bias stage after detecting the voltage fluctuation of the amplifier, and the quiescent current recovers to low levels in the steady state. The proposed LDO is implemented in the TSMC 180 nm process, and the simulation results show that the quiescent current of LDO is about 1.8 μA. When the load current varies between 100 μA and 10mA within 500 ns, the overshoot and undershoot voltages are 16mV and 140 mV, respectively, and the recovery time is 202 ns.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Calibration Technique for Capacitor Mismatch in SAR ADCs
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents an insightful analysis of split capacitor digital-to-analog converter (CDAC) error in a successive-approximation-register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). A novel model is proposed to explain the capacitor mismatch induced error, and then two classic calibration techniques, which are called low-to-high (L2H) end and high-to-low (H2L) herein, are also reviewed. With the accurate analysis and the model, we present a calibration technique exemplified in a 12-bit SAR ADC with split-CDAC. Behavioral simulation shows that the proposed calibration is capable of correcting mismatch errors and “segment error” of split-CDAC array. It improves the spurious free dynamic range (SFDR) from 55.8 to 95.5 dB in a 12 bit split-CDAC SAR ADC using a behavior model.

articleTitle: A Near-Field Super-Resolution THz Sensor Utilizing Micro-Coaxial Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a super-resolution near-field sensing probe designed by micro-coaxial. Utilizing waveguide micro-coaxial to confine terahertz (THz) waves within transmission lines and guide them to the tip of a probe, which can effectively enhance the dynamic range and reduce transmission losses in free space. It is designed for easy integration, with probe dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.9}\ \mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{0.9}\ \mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{5.4}\ \mathbf{mm}$</tex>. The sensor designed operates at 90 GHz realizing spatial resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{20}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>, about 1/165 of a wavelength. This sensor can achieve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{100}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> response distance and 16 dB dynamic range, respectively. Micro-coaxial probes utilize copper as the metal conductor and air as the dielectric materials of transmission.

articleTitle: 109.9-dB DR and 17.9-Bit ENOB Dynamic Zoom CDC Design for Audio Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Capacitive sensors are one of the most widely used sensors today. In recent years, High resolution has assumed a paramount role in sensor design, guaranteeing precise measurement outcomes. Quantification to the aF level is urgently needed. This paper presents the first dynamic Zoom capacitance to digital converter (CDC) incorporating noise coupling (NC) technology, which is intended for high-precision sensor applications in the audio domain. The proposed dynamic CDC is a hybrid of a high-resolution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{\Delta}\mathbf{\Sigma}$</tex> modulator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{\Delta}\mathbf{\Sigma}\mathbf{M})$</tex> and a high-efficiency SAR-based CDC to achieve better performance. It is implemented in the TSMC 180 nm process, and the simulation results show that it achieves 109.9dB DR and 109.3dB SNR within the bandwidth of 20kHz, consuming <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{81}\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{W}$</tex> from a 1.2V supply. These advancements are accomplished through the combined utilization of coarse and fine conversions, noise coupling techniques, SAR-assisted multi-bit quantizers, and operational transconductance amplifiers (OTAs) based on dynamic bias inverters.

articleTitle: A Broad-Bandwidth Cascode-Feedback Transimpedance Amplifier for Short-Range Optical Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Recently, demands in short-range optical communications with high integration are increasing very fast, and transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs) play a significant role in optical communication systems. This paper presents a broad-bandwidth TIA, which investigates the design strategy of the regulated cascode (RGC) TIA under low supply voltage. The proposed TIA includes a cascode-feedback RGC input stage with transistors working in weak inversion to achieve an optimized trade-off among bandwidth, low supply, power consumption and noise. Capacitive degeneration is used to further extend the bandwidth. In 40-nm CMOS, the proposed TIA under 1.2 V can achieve a -3dB bandwidth of 8.65 GHz with 0.25 pF photodiode capacitance and 0.15 pF load capacitance. The total input-referred noise current is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2.47}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{A}$</tex>. The core TIA occupies 0.003 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> while the DC power consumption is 2.46 mW without the output buffer. Compared with related TIA works, the proposed TIA achieves comparable bandwidth performance and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2}\times\sim \mathbf{3.5}\times$</tex> figure of merit enhancement.

articleTitle: An Improved MDAC for High-Speed Pipeline ADCs Application
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce an improved multiply digital-to-analog converter (MDAC) for high-speed and high-resolution pipelined analog-to-digital converter (ADC) applications. The proposed technique, without increasing power consumption and noise, can enable devices of all key analog modules in MDAC to use thin-oxide MOS transistors with minimum channel length to meet the speed requirements of ADC and avoid the breakdown problem of these MOSFETs under high output common-mode voltages of Op-amp or SHA. This work is implemented in 28nm mixture signal CMOS process. The MDAC can achieve 49dB loop gain and 7.89GHz loop bandwidth at 30mW power consumption in 8-bit 2.5Gs/s pipelined ADC applications.

articleTitle: Geometric Parameter Optimization of Underbrink Array Based on Response Surface Method
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In the recent years, the Underbrink array is one of the most frequently used planar arrays for acoustic imaging. However, there is no guidance for the array to select geometric parameters. In this paper, by applying the response surface method to Underbrink array, we propose a new method to decide the geometric parameters. First, we build a regression model of the width of the main lobe with respect to the geometric parameters of the Underbrink array including the number of microphones, the number of helical arms, and the aperture of the array. Then, according to the constructed regression model, the value range of a parameter can be determined to obtain the optimal parameter combination in this range. Simulation results show that, by exploiting the proposed method, we obtain better geometry parameters for the Underbrink array.

articleTitle: Digital Image Processing System Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper proposes a digital image processing system that uses FPGA to process color images into black and white images and outlines the edge lines of objects. And the digital image processing system is used to recognize printed numbers through feature discrimination. The digital image processing system built by FPGA has the characteristics of simple structure, high real-time performance, low-frequency requirement, and high integration. This is not only suitable for high-speed real-time systems, but also saves hardware resources to a great extent, and significantly reduces design costs. The realization of this paper is to capture the RGB565 format image by the camera and convert it into the YCbCr format image, and then project the image in the horizontal and vertical directions and then perform feature discrimination on the captured numbers. Finally, the result is output through the digital tube.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Strip-Line Filter and Duplexer with the Mixed Electromagnetic Couplings
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method is proposed to introduce the mixed electromagnetic coupling into the design of metal strip-line filter. The transmission zeros generated by the mixed electromagnetic coupling are flexible and controllable, on the basis of the existing cross-coupled filter, more transmission zeros are introduced to improve the frequency selection characteristics of the filter, and achieve the purpose of filter miniaturization. To verify the effectiveness of this method, according to the synthesis theory of cross-coupled filters with the mixed electromagnetic coupling, we designed a 3.5G filter and a 2.6G duplexer, the synthesis results, and the simulation results are well matched, which reveals the effectiveness of the presented method.

articleTitle: An Ultra- Low Power Robust- Startup Class-C DCO Achieving -191.4 dB FoM
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Ultra-low-power (ULP) transceivers (TRXs) have been key elements in a variety of short-range network applications. The phase locked loop (PLL) provides local oscillating signals in TRXs which consumes lots of power to meet up with the phase noise requirement. Digital-controlled-oscillator (DCO) is the key building module in all-digital-PLL (ADPLL) which determines the out-band phase noise performance. This paper presents a robust startup complementary Class-C DCO by switching the gate voltage of the cross-coupled NMOS transistors, which achieves low phase noise with ultra-low power consumption. The proposed switching circuit mainly includes a RS latch and two comparators operating at a low frequency clock to reduce power consuming. The tuning bank consists of 5-bit coarse capacitors array, 128 medium capacitors and 32 fine capacitors to obtain a 2.2 GHz ~2.6 GHz frequency tuning range. The proposed DCO is implemented on a 40 nm CMOS process. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DCO has a 20% tuning range and phase noise of -120.4 dBc/Hz @ 1MHz with a 2.4 GHz carrier frequency while consuming <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{450}\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{W}$</tex> from a 1.1-V supply, yielding a Figure-of-Merit (FoM) of −191.4 dB.

articleTitle: A Second Harmonic Amplitude Conversion Circuit for Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper proposes a second harmonic amplitude conversion circuit for power amplifier, the operating frequency band of this conversion circuit ranges from 5.5 GHz to 6 GHz. In order to reduce the complexity of signal processing encountered by digital pre-distortion technology, the circuit proposed in this paper is based on the injection-locked frequency divider, and proportionally convert the signal amplitude at second harmonic frequency into the signal amplitude at fundamental frequency. Using this technology, the second harmonic distortion signal could be observed through the injection-locked frequency divider output signal. Therefore, it could effectively reduce the complexity of the digital pre-distortion signal processing. The circuit simulation results show that for an input signal with a frequency of 11.6G, a frequency of 5.8G signal which proportional to the amplitude of the input signal is generated at the output.

articleTitle: A Novel Voltage-Gated Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetic Non-Volatile Binary Content-Addressable Memory Cell for High-Reliable Search and Low-Power Write Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel magnetic non-volatile binary content-addressable memory (MNV-BCAM) cell. In this cell, two MTJs in complementary resistive state are used to store 1-bit information and the emerging voltage-gated spin-orbit torque (VGSOT) effect is employed to achieve low-power write operation. As for its search operation, one differential sense amplifier (DSA) is employed, which is envisioned to achieve high reliability and low power consumption. Additionally, by using only one transistor as the critical path between the match-line and GND, the proposed MNV-BCAM cell can achieve fast search operation. Hybrid CMOS/MTJ simulation results of the 144-bit word circuit show that the proposed MNV-BCAM cell can achieve small search error rate of 1%, small search delay of 0.91 ns, low search energy dissipation of 0.5 fJ/bit/search, small write delay of 1.3 ns and energy dissipation of 3.8 fJ/bit.

articleTitle: An 8-GHz Bandwidth Push-Pull Input Buffer Based on Cascode Source Follower
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband and high linearity input buffer based on a pseudo-differential complementary push-pull structure with drain bootstrapped, implemented with 28-nm CMOS process. The buffer is designed with a push-pull structure that has a wide bandwidth and low output impedance. Furthermore, the drains of the output transistors are bootstrapped to suppress channel length modulation effects. The level shifter circuits are utilized to bias the NMOS and PMOS devices of the push-pull structure, enabling them to operate in the saturation region. Due to device mismatch, a common-mode feedback circuit is used to stabilize the DC operating point for stable operation. The proposed input buffer has a power consumption of 100mW under a 1.8V power supply and demonstrates high linearity and wide bandwidth.

articleTitle: An Automated Calibration Scheme for PLL in Time-to-Digital Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In high performance Time-to-Digital Converters (TDCs), PLL can be adopted to generate the required reference clock, which is in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 100 \ \text{MHz}$</tex> range. In order to improve the phase noise performance, the full VCO frequency range in such a PLL is generally divided into multiple sectors, which can be selected by digital code. This paper proposes an automated calibration scheme to set the digital code for optimized VCO performance. Primarily based on successive approximation algorithm, the proposed scheme completes the automated calibration with only minimal steps. By co-simulating with a typical PLL, the efficacy of the proposed scheme is fully validated. Tentatively synthesized using CMOS 180nm technology, the automated calibration scheme only occupies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100\times 100\text{um}^{2}$</tex> of silicon area, and consists of 144 logical gates. The power consumption is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 100\ \text{uW}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Multi-layer BiLSTM Photovoltaic Prediction Study Based on Improved PSO
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In order to improve prediction accuracy of photovoltaic (PV) power output, this paper proposes a multilayer bi-directional long-and short-term memory (BiLSTM) based on improved particle swarm (PSO) for PV power prediction. Firstly, according to timing-related characteristics of PV power generation, a multilayer BiLSTM model is constructed to learn hidden PV power data information. Secondly, in order to improve efficiency of model training, improved PSO algorithm is constructed. Particle information is initialized using inverse learning and dynamic inertia weighting strategy is utilized to improve performance of algorithm parameter tuning. Finally, multilayer BiLSTM model based on improved PSO predicts PV power. Simulation example analysis shows that the proposed method can significantly improve prediction accuracy of PV power.

articleTitle: A 2.036ppm/°C Bandgap Reference with Novel Piecewise Curvature Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this study, a novel piecewise curvature compensation circuit was presented for a bandgap reference. In order to significantly reduce the temperature drift of the reference voltage, the novel piecewise curvature compensation circuit adjusts the relative values of the positive and negative temperature-coefficient current to control the temperature threshold of the compensation current. A negative feedback structure is utilized to provide a bias voltage for cascode current mirror, which gives the reference voltage high power supply rejection ratio (PSRR). The bandgap reference circuit is designed using 1.8 V supply voltage and 0.18 um TSMC CMOS technology. Simulation results show that the temperature coefficient of the reference voltage is 2.036 ppm/°C in the typical process corner and 3.416 ppm/°C in the worst process corner over the range of -40°C to 130°C. The PSRR can reach 80dB (10 Hz) across each corner. The circuit consumes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$109\ \mu \mathrm{W}$</tex> in total.

articleTitle: A Vertical Transition Structure in K-Band for Tile Transmitter-Receiver Module
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, a wide band vertical transition structure operating in K-band, composed of bond wire and via, suitable for tile transmitter-receiver (TR) module is presented. By analyzing the parasitic effects of bond wire and via, we adjusted the shape and size of pad and anti-pad belonging to the via to introduce distributed capacitance to offset the parasitic inductance of bond wire and via. The results show that return loss more than 10 dB and insertion loss less than 0.6dB was obtained from 20GHz to 30GHZ. Also, in order to guide the design and processing of the actual circuit, we also studied the effect of the arch height and diameter of bond wire on the signal transition. It can be seen that the lower the arch height and the larger the diameter result in smaller insertion loss.

articleTitle: A 22-Bit 34-uW Sturdy-MASH Digital Delta-Sigma Modulator with Nested Bus-Splitting and Resolution Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In response to the power consumption and precision requirements of Digital Delta-Sigma Modulators (DDSMs) used in digital-to-analog converters (DACs), this paper proposes a sturdy-Multi stAge noise SHaping (MASH) DDSM structure based on nested bus-splitting and resolution enhancement techniques. This work utilized the TSMC 40nm CMOS standard cell and completed the logic synthesis using Synopsys Design Compiler, and its functionality and performance were verified in FPGA board. The results show that compared to state-of-the-art designs, this structure approximately saves 15% of hardware consumption and improves Effective Number of Bits (ENOB) by 2.36 bits.

articleTitle: A Wide Linear Range Ultra-low Transconductance Amplifier for Biomedical Sensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In the field of biomedical sensors, active filters with very low cutoff frequencies are required because of the weak electrical signals from the human body. The Gm-C filters are more prominent among the filter designs, which consist of an operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) and a capacitor. The key design issues are transconductance and linearity. In this paper, a new ultra-low transconductance OTA structure is proposed. The basic idea is to extend the linear input range of the OTA using the source degeneration pseudo-resistor technique and the bulk-driven technique. The transconductance is reduced by using series-parallel current mirrors for the OTA. This ultra-low transconductance OTA has an extremely low bias current of 0.1nA and a shunt factor of 100, reducing the OTA transconductance to 0.4pS with 39.55μVrms noise. It also increases the linear input range from ±50mV to ±2.5V, extending it by a factor of 50.

articleTitle: A low-noise, high-precision chopper instrument amplifier for EEG signal amplification
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, a low-noise, high-precision chopper instrumentation amplifier (IA) for EEG signal acquisition and amplification is designed. To achieve low-noise performance, chopper modulation is applied. A common-mode compensation structure is designed for chopper modulation application environment, which makes the overall performance of IA more stable. At 1000x amplification, the equivalent input noise is only 25.3nV/sqrt(Hz)@10Hz, CMRR is 155.3dB, PSRR is 167.5dB, offset is only 10.26uV, and input impedance is 10.7GΩ@100HZ.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Positive and Negative Dual-Output Charge Pump
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: An adaptive positive and negative dual-output charge pump circuit is developed based on the traditional positive and negative dual-output charge pump (CP) circuit through load monitoring and dynamic adjustment of the transistors used for the pump capacitors charging. Firstly, the circuit's driving ability is enhanced by alternately charging and discharging capacitor using different transistors. Furthermore, the boosted positive output voltage serves directly as a power supply for generating the negative output. Finally, the utilization of large transistors for charging the pump capacitor under heavy load and small transistors under light load enables the sustained output of the CP, eliminating the adverse effects of intermittent pumping on response speed and output ripple. It also reduces power consumption under light load conditions when using small transistors for charging the pump capacitor, consequently leading to higher conversion efficiency. The proposed adaptive positive and negative dual-output CP circuit is designed based on the SMIC 180 nm process, with a chip area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1656} \ast \mathbf{637}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}\mathbf{2}$</tex>. Simulation results show that the circuit achieves an efficiency above 80% within a load current range of 0–120 mA.

articleTitle: Design of Identity Recognition System Based on Multi-Dimensional Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-dimensional information fusion identification system is proposed, which integrates face recognition, voice print recognition, fingerprint recognition and RFID recognition. Based on multi-dimensional information, the user identity is recognized, and the identification security is improved. Finally, the system is simulated and tested, and the feasibility of the system is verified.

articleTitle: Research on Blockchain Based Electric Carbon Intelligent Collaborative Carbon Verification Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper uses blockchain distributed storage, immutable, peer-to-peer network and other technical characteristics. Based on the greenhouse gas accounting methods of all industries released by the state, the paper uses electricity data such as online electricity quantity and purchased electricity quantity to build a electric carbon intelligent collaborative carbon verification platform, and carries out carbon emission, carbon verification and monitoring from the technical verification. The collaborative management and application mode of power grid enterprises, government departments, emission control enterprises and third-party verification institutions shall be formed, so as to establish a multi-party trust mechanism, realize online business handling, peer-to-peer information transparency, reliable data tamper-proof, and effectively improve carbon verification efficiency, mutual trust and user satisfaction.

articleTitle: A 6.1-nW, 4.3-kHz, -40-90°C Relaxation Oscillator for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper proposed a relaxation oscillator (RxO) with an extended operating range achieved through the implementation of a subthreshold leakage current compensation (SLC) technique. The compensated RxO outperforms the uncompensated counterpart by 25 times for temperature coefficient (TC). Moreover, its performance is further optimized using a forward body bias (FBB) technique, resulting in a 30% delay reduction for the buffer at low supply voltage. Designed in a 65nm CMOS process, the proposed RxO consumes 6.1 nW under a 0.4 V supply at 4.3 kHz, achieving an energy efficiency of 1.42 nW/kHz at room temperature. The oscillator exhibits TC of 100.4 ppm/°C across a temperature range from -40°C to 90°C, making it a prospective choice for low-power Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: A Solution Method for Non-Smooth Wirelength Model of VLSI Overall Layout Based on Neiderreit Sequence Initialized Harris Hawk Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: The layout method of very large scale integration (VLSI) is the top priority of its physical design and the core issue of electronic design automation (EDA) technology. It is also the most upstream, high-end and strategic part in the integrated circuit industry. The layout algorithm for VLSI typically includes3 steps: overall layout, layout legalization, and detailed layout, and the quality of the overall layout will directly affect the quality of the final layout. As overall layout is the key to the success in solving layout problems for VLSI, in this paper, the non-smooth and non-convex optimization problem formed by the non-smooth wirelength model of VLSI overall layout has been studied. Different from the existing methods in solving such non-smooth optimization problem based on subgradient descent (SubGD) method or conjugate subgradient (CSG) method, which are easy to fall into the trap of local minimum, in this paper, a. derivative-free optimization method based on Neiderreit sequence initialized Harris hawk optimization (NSHHO) algorithm has been proposed and applied. Numerical experiments have shown that NSHHO is more effective than those common methods that rely on subgradient information.

articleTitle: A Spatiotemporal Coding Letters Recognition Circuit Based on Organic Neuromorphic Synaptic Transistor
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: With the rapid development of the artificial intelligence and big data technology, data centers need to throughput and process massive data information under immense pressure. Low power and efficient parallel data processing still face significant challenges. In this work, we propose a spatiotemporal coding letters recognition (SCLR) circuit system based on an organic neuromorphic synaptic transistor (ONST) as the front-end reservoir computing (RC) device combined with the back-end feedback type trans-impedance amplifier (TIA), successive approximation register (SAR) ADC circuit and MCU module for efficient spatiotemporal information processing in real-time. The dynamic conductance inhibition process caused by the holes trapping behavior in the front-end RC device allows the ONST to preserve the memory information of the input signal. The back-end circuit modules can realize the functions of current-to-voltage conversion and voltage amplification., and the correct letter output can be achieved by the MCU. Our work potentially paves a way in the field of the future low-power consumption intelligent edge machine vision system.

articleTitle: Modeling and optimization of local oscillation signals for Nyquist Folding Receiver
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Sensing broadband spectrum using a low-speed analog-to-digital converter is a challenge for reconnaissance receivers. Nyquist Folding Receiver (NYFR) proposed by Fudge's team, as one of the effective sub-Nyquist sampling schemes exhibits a lower system working frequency than most other schemes. NYFR relies on a local oscillation signal(LOS) to generate periodic non-uniform sampling pulses. The design of the LOS directly affects the system's overall performance, yet few studies are currently available. In this paper, we study the working model of the LOS, analyze several elements that affect the sampling performance, and optimize the LOS by taking the performance indexes as constraints. Theoretical derivations and simulation experiments show that the optimized LOS in this paper can produce better NYFR sampling waveforms with strong broadband signal processing capability and system robustness.

articleTitle: A Low Power High Swing Charge Pump for Phase Locked Loops
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a low power high swing charge pump for phase-locked loop (PLL) applications. The charge pump achieves low power consumption by using three switch circuits to allow one operational amplifier (OPA) to be used in both charge and discharge current mirror circuits on demand, thus the power consumption is greatly reduced and both charge and discharge current mirrors can achieve high impedance with the use of the multiplexed OPA, resulting in the charge pump exhibiting a high swing output. The charge pump is designed in 40nm CMOS process and verified under 1.2 V voltage supply, simulation results demonstrate that the designed charge pump achieves a power consumption of only 159 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{W}$</tex>, while meeting high output swing requirements of 89 mV to 1.06 V when the current mismatch rate is less than 1%, the switch time is less than 10 ps and the phase noise is -116 dBc/Hz@1MHz.

articleTitle: High-Side PMOS Driving Half-Bridge Driver with a Higher Turn-Off Rate
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: The traditional High-Side PMOS driving bridge driver exhibits a fast turn-on and slow turn-off phenomenon when driving the external high-side PMOS, which eventually causes the output pulse to broaden. This phenomenon occurs because of the characteristics of the PMOS, turning off slower than turning on. To solve the above problem, a new method is proposed to enhance the voltage difference of the PMOS by raising the turn-off voltage, which is far beyond the turn-off threshold of the PMOS, so the PMOS can be turn-off quickly. A High-Side PMOS driving half-bridge driver IC is designed and fabricated by using a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.18}\ \mu\ \mathbf{m}$</tex> BCD chip process flow. The application of the IC as a test board is also fabricated. The verification results show that the pulse width of the signal varies by only 5.5 ns.

articleTitle: A staggered-arrangement EBG decoupling structure for Ku-band vehicle-mounted antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Ku-band (10.7-12.7GHz) vehicle-mounted mobile antenna serves as a link to satellite communication networks, which are widely used in applications such as mobile news, emergency response, and remote work. However, the electromagnetic interference and mutual coupling could disrupt the antenna performance and degrade the communication quality when it integrates multiple antennas on a vehicle platform, which is caused by the excitation and propagation of surface waves between adjacent antennas. A choke slot is commonly employed to enhance the isolation between antennas, but it diverges from the trend toward integrated circuitry and flat design in communication system development. Therefore, this paper presents a novel staggered-arrangement electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structure designed on current distribution, which can effectively enhance the overall isolation level to 70 dB within the frequency range of 10.7-12.7 GHz in simulation, and realize the integration of antenna and isolation structure into circuit system. The EBG with high isolation alleviates electromagnetic interference among antennas, ensuring the consistent functionality of vehicle-mounted antennas and improving communication quality.

articleTitle: A Low Voltage and Ultra-low Power Reference Circuit for Passive UHF RFID Tag Chip
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper describes a low voltage and ultra-low power reference circuit to generate voltage reference and current reference for passive UHF RFID tag chip based on subthreshold CMOS. It adds the threshold voltage with negative temperature coefficient (TC) and the thermal voltage with positive TC, to produce reference voltage and current with zero TC. The voltage reference circuit outputs voltage of 411 mV, featuring a TC of 17.1 ppm/°C to 43.1 ppm/°C from -25°C to 100 °C. And the current reference outputs 101 nA of current with a TC of 15.4 ppm/°C to 115.8 ppm/°C. The power consumption of voltage reference and current reference are 188.1 nW and 366.3nW. Because there is multiplexing of circuits, the total power consumption is 463 nW, and 513 nW at worst.

articleTitle: A High-Speed and Low-Noise Charge Pump for PLL
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper introduces a high-speed and low-noise charge pump for phase-locked loop. The use of low-voltage switch increases the turn-on and turn-off speed and charge pump can operate at 300 MHz. The output current range of the charge pump is 2-30mA in 2mA steps and the current mismatch less than 0.5%. The phase noise is -223.2 dBA/Hz@1MHz at 2 mA and -206.6 dBA/Hz@10KHz at 30 mA.

articleTitle: Optimizing Battery Discharge with Supercapacitor: Design, Evaluation and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: IoT devices will inevitably generate large current loads during operation, which will reduce the available capacity of the battery. Using supercapacitor to buffer large current loads helps optimize battery capacity utilization. However, there is a lack of in-depth research on the interaction between the battery and supercapacitor in existing works. To address this issue, this paper constructs a circuit that permits adjustable configuration of hybrid power supply and conducts a preliminary analysis of the performance of hybrid power supply and the primary parameters influencing its performance. Experimental results reveal that retaining the supercapacitor linked to the battery causes wasteful loss of battery capacity due to self-discharge of the supercapacitor, especially under duty cycled loads. Therefore, it is necessary to comprehensively consider the rate capacity effect of battery and the self-discharge characteristics of supercapacitor in order to maximize the utilization of battery capacity.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency and Low-Ripple Boost Charge Pump
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: A high-efficiency and low-ripple charge pump structure is proposed to address the problems of severe voltage losses and high output ripple of conventional charge pumps. The charge pump uses a deep n-well process and a substrate biasing circuit to reduce voltage losses and improve conversion efficiency. And the upper and lower two parallel branches are used to reduce the output ripple, while the pre-charging process is carried out to shorten the start-up time. The charge pump is designed based on the SMIC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.11}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> CMOS process, and the final simulation results show that the charge pump can achieve an output voltage of 2.85V with a ripple of only about 1mV at an input voltage of 1.5V and a load of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{\Omega}$</tex>. This charge pump has the advantages of high conversion efficiency and regulated output, and can be widely used in electronic products such as Bluetooth headset and lithium battery.

articleTitle: A 6-9.3GHz Low Phase Noise Quad-Core LC VCO in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, a quad-core LC VCO design is implemented in 65nm CMOS process, with the tuning range from 6 to 9.3 GHz (45%). In this design, four identical VCO cores are coupled synchronously, which breaks through the minimum phase noise limit of a single VCO. Source inductance filtering technology is used in each VCO core to suppress the second harmonic of current source transistor injection tank. The phase noise performance of -137.7MHz is realized under the frequency offset of 1MHz at 7GHz. The VCO consumes 200mW power with the figure-of-merit(FOM) of 192.8 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset.

articleTitle: A Global Routing Algorithm for PCB Based on Triangular Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Global routing is a critical problem in PCB routing, and its quality greatly affect the PCB design cost. Unlike existing methods based on traditional rectangular grid, this paper present a novel algorithm based on triangular grid model to handle the problem. We first propose a method to sort all the unconnected two-pin nets, then construct a triangular grid graph to represent the routing resources on the printed circuited board. Finally we use the idea of maximum flow to find the paths to complete global routing and use the detailed routing to get the result of completed wires. Experimental results show that our algorithm can spend less time than the two state-of-the-art routers without any design rule violations for all given industrial PCB instances.

articleTitle: Research on Capacitance Array Method Applied to 12 bits SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Capacitor array is very important in the research of SAR ADC (Successive Approximation ADC), its area,matching, noise, power consumption and other performance will determine the conversion performance of the entire ADC. This paper firstly analyzes the value of unit capacitance theoretically, determines the calculation method of unit capacitance value, and then designs five layout structures of unit capacitance, and respectively analyzes the capacitance array layout composed of five kinds of unit capacitors PEX (Parasitic Extraction) and Post- Simulation. After comparing the simulation results, the best structure was selected and further optimized. Finally, based on the SMIC 0.18um CMOS process library, the optimized unit capacitor layout was selected to design a DAC capacitor array layout that can be used for 12 bits SAR ADC. The final capacitor array uses five layers of metal M1-M5, with a length of 220um, a width of 85um, and an area of 18700um<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A 12-Bit Voltage DAC Based on Dual 8-Bit Resistive Divider DACs
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: A 12-bit voltage digital-to-analog converter (DAC) based on a dual 8-bit resistive divider DACs is proposed. The resistor ladder structure is used to achieve two 8-bit DACs. Then, analog addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division operations are performed on the outputs of the two 8-bit DACs, achieving a final 12-bit DAC output voltage. The circuit structure is simple, it only uses a total of 512 resistors, avoiding the problem of requiring a larger area and being susceptible to process mismatch as in traditional structures that use 4096 resistors. The proposed 12-bit voltage DAC is designed using HHGRACE 110nm process, and the entire area is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.144\ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. The post-simulation results show that, under typical process and temperature conditions, the simulated DNL is −0.17~0.13 LSB, INL is −0.06~0.23 LSB, SFDR is 87.7734 dB, and ENOB is 11.8604 bits.

articleTitle: An 8×28Gb/s Serializer with 2-Tap SST Driver in 65nm CMOS for Chiplet Optical I/O
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 28\text{Gb}/\mathrm{s}$</tex> serializer with 2-tap FFE for the chiplet optical I/Os in 65nm CMOS. A simplified direct-multiplexing topology is proposed based-on the multi-phase clock, which eliminates the power-hungry latches at high-speed. A 2-tap SST driver is employed to save static power and provide up to 29dB EQ. A T-line based clock distribution circuit is proposed with triple inductive peaking, which delivers the 14GHz clock across 3000μm distance with low power. The proposed serializer has been implemented in a 65-nm CMOS process, achieving an energy efficiency of 4.48 pJ/bit. Experimental results show it achieves 28Gb/s channel speed on a 6dB loss PCB channel, achieving 523mV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</inf> voltage swing, 1.5ps RMS jitter, while occupying only 0.1mm2 area per channel.
